newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurd group fires at rival despite ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group fires at rival despite ceasefire.

text.p: A Kurdish militia fired shells and Katyusha rockets at a rival group in northern Iraq on Thursday, nine hours after a U.S.-brokered ceasefire was supposed to come into effect, witnesses said.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) opened fire sporadically on Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) fighters near the town of Degala at 9 a.m. (0500 GMT), they said.
"There is no sign of a ceasefire," leading KDP commander Roj Nuri Shuwayis told Reuters. His forces did not fire back.

The PUK said earlier that its forces had been ordered to stop fighting. "There were orders to that effect on the ground yesterday because we were expecting (the ceasefire), but we haven't been in contact with Iraqi Kurdistan this morning," said Shazad Saib, the PUK's Turkey's representative.
The U.S. State Department announced that the groups had agreed to observe a ceasefire beginning at midnight Iraqi time (2000 GMT on Wednesday).
The bombardment prevented U.N. officials from travelling to the PUK-held town of Koy Sanjak to organise a relief convoy of food and medicine from the city of Arbil, under KDP control.
"We can't go through because of the firing. We have enough food for the starving people of Koy Sanjak but we can't get through to help them," a senior U.N. official said in Degala.

U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau got an agreement to halt the fighting from the two factions' leaders at separate meetings in Turkey this week. The clashes have damaged U.S. interests in northern Iraq and threatened to draw in Iraq and Iran.
Iraqi troops and tanks helped the KDP capture Arbil from the PUK on August 31, prompting retaliatory U.S. missile strikes against Iraqi military targets.
